abstract: Bacteriophages capable of propagating in host cells that have entered or are approaching the early stationary phase of growth (eSPI phages) are promising candidates for phage therapy as they may efficiently destroy slowly growing pathogen populations in vivo. Among the Escherichia coli phages, the eSPI phenotype is rare and the diversity of such phages is limited. Siphoviruses of the Dhillonvirus genus appear to offer an attractive platform for implementing host range management systems. We investigated the structure of the eSPI Dhillonvirus DH23 using cryo-electron microscopy and single-particle analysis and revealed that its adaptor protein connecting the dodecameric head portal to the hexamer ring of the tail termination protein forms a tridecameric (C13) ring rather than a dodecameric ring as in most known bacteriophages. Despite the presence of the putative lateral tail fiber (LTF) protein gene in the DH23 genome, the tail tip 3D density map showed no evidence of LTF attachment. Examination of 2D projection images of the flexible distal part of the central tail fiber (CTF) revealed a massive density from which the LTFs emanate, forming a branched CTF-LTF structure that was not seen in coliphages previously.
